title: Security review - pen test results & patching cadence - Aurora Finance
summary: Review of recent pen test findings and agreement on patching cadence and secure SDLC steps. Action items: share detailed pen test spreadsheet, patch schedule, and RBAC/SSO configuration guide.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Chen (Redwood SA), Priya Kaur (Aurora Security Lead), Mark DeVries (Aurora CTO), Liam O'Connor (Aurora IT Ops), Sofia Ramos (Aurora Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — Jordan here, AE on the account, with Samir and Ava from our security/solutions team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Kaur: good, thanks. we circulated the pen test report earlier, appreciate you carving out time to walk through details.
[00:15] Mark DeVries: yes — main thing for us is to understand exposure windows and patching cadence, also how redwood's hosted vs dedicated impacts our remediation responsibility.
[00:25] Samir Patel: absolutely. we'll run through the high-level findings, clarify which ones are in-scope for the redwood runtime vs customer app layer, and propose timelines. note: transcript may have some auto-correct errors on acronyms, sorry in advance.
[00:36] Ava Chen: quick note — we also brought SOC2 and ISO docs to discuss audit log retention and encryption defaults.

[02:00] Samir Patel: ok starting with finding one — auth bypass vector reported on the demo environment. pen tester found a missing validation header that could allow session token replay in our test harness. severity marked as high by the test team.
[02:22] Priya Kaur: that's the one we were most worried about, yeah. can you confirm if that was on hosted api or on the customer-managed integration?
[02:30] Samir Patel: from our investigation it's specific to the demo harness they spun up against our public sandbox. our production-hosted API uses strict session validation and short lived tokens; that demo harness had an older sample client that didn't enforce the new header. so responsibility: remediation is on our side to update the sample clients and sandbox configs. for customer-managed private deployments, you control the client.
[02:55] Mark DeVries: ok that's helpful — so production hosted customers not impacted?
[03:02] Ava Chen: correct, production hosted has the header validation, logs show 401s for malformed requests. we're going to patch the sandbox templates and rotate any example tokens.

[05:10] Priya Kaur: second item — dependency vuln in an older CUDA driver used in a dedicated node image in you folks' marketplace AMI. pen test flagged it as medium with exploit potential.
[05:25] Samir Patel: yep we saw that. the dedicated image we provide is updated monthly, but some customers pin older images. we maintain a CVE tracking board; images in our default pool rotated last week to a patched driver, but pinned images will need an explicit patch.
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: when you say "pinned images" — how do we get notified? what's the cadence for pushing critical kernel/driver patches to dedicated fleets?
[05:55] Ava Chen: critical patches are pushed as hotfixes when severity >= critical (CVSS 9+). for high/medium we recommend a rolling patch schedule; we also provide a notification feed and can open a support ticket for targeted fleets.
[06:15] Priya Kaur: can we get an SLA for patch windows on dedicated? our compliance team wants defined times.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: we can include a dedicated patch SLA in the Dedicated contract addendum — Samir, capture that as an action item.

[08:00] Samir Patel: third item — KMS key usage and key residency. pen tester probed key wrapping endpoints. they flagged lack of explicit customer-managed key enforcement in hosted default.
[08:12] Sofia Ramos: so by default hosted customers don't get a customer-managed key? we need all keys to be customer-controlled for PCI scope reduction.
[08:20] Ava Chen: by default hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS for ease of onboarding. we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated and Private, and for hosted we offer KMS integration for enterprise customers on request. we'll provide docs and a plan to enable CMK for Aurora.
[08:40] Priya Kaur: timeline to enable CMK on hosted? we have a short window to reduce PCI scope.
[08:46] Samir Patel: we can enable CMK on your account as a configuration change; lead time usually 3-5 business days to validate metadata and key rotation policies. action item for Samir to start onboarding.

[10:30] Mark DeVries: a question on audit logs — retention and format. pen test said some request-level logs were truncated in the sandbox. what's production behaviour?
[10:40] Ava Chen: production retains request/response metadata and full audit trails for control-plane actions for 90 days by default, with extended retention add-ons. some customer tokens/PII are scrubbed from payloads by default; we capture headers, timestamps, model/version, and token counts. we can export logs to customer S3 or SIEM.
[11:05] Priya Kaur: we need >1 year retention for certain logs for forensics, and export to our secure S3 in EU. can you support that?
[11:14] Ava Chen: yes — log export and region residency supported via our Private control plane or enterprise hosted region configs. we'll provide the export playbook.

[13:00] Samir Patel: vulnerability management process overview: we triage incoming findings with our SecOps, severity assigned by CVSS and business impact, then owners are identified in our JIRA board. P1/Critical go to a paged on-call, P2 go into the next sprint or hotfix depending on impact.
[13:28] Priya Kaur: do you share the triage timeline publicly per customer? we need visibility for audit.
[13:36] Jordan Lee: we can provide a customer-facing remediation tracker for enterprise accounts showing status and expected remediation dates.

[15:00] Liam O'Connor: patching cadence question again — what's the typical maintenance window for dedicated nodes? we want minimal downtime.
[15:08] Samir Patel: for dedicated pools we do rolling reboots across nodes, typically 2-4 hours per node depending on model warm-up time. we have fast failover; clients using KV cache/sequence state may need to reconnect but we maintain session continuity for short windows.
[15:30] Mark DeVries: how about hotpatching without reboot? can kernels/drivers be live-patched?
[15:36] Ava Chen: some vendor kernel live-patches are possible, but GPU driver major upgrades require node restarts. we minimize impact with gradual draining and can schedule during your low-traffic windows.

[18:00] Priya Kaur: secure SDLC — pen tester noted missing threat modeling in one internal service. what is your secure development lifecycle?
[18:10] Samir Patel: we follow a secure SDLC: threat modeling during design for customer-impacting features, static analysis as part of CI, dependency scanning in build pipeline, and mandatory security review for release. we'll share the devsecops checklist.
[18:26] Priya Kaur: can you include evidence (JIRA tickets, scan outputs) for audits?
[18:32] Ava Chen: yes we can provide audit artifacts on request as part of our compliance pack.

[22:00] Jordan Lee: ok circling back — for each high/critical finding we've categorized owners: Redwood-run sandbox issues -> Redwood to patch; Dedicated-image issues -> we publish patched image and notify pinned customers; hosted default KMS -> enable CMK for Aurora; audit log retention -> export playbook; SDLC evidence -> compliance pack.

[24:15] Priya Kaur: on remediation timelines — what's realistic for high/critical?
[24:22] Samir Patel: critical: 48-72 hours turnaround for mitigation/hotfix, high: 1-2 weeks depending on regression risk and testing. medium: next release cycle or scheduled patch. we'll put specific ETA per finding in the spreadsheet.

[28:00] Mark DeVries: question about RBAC and SSO — we want role separation between dev and ops and a way to restrict access to logs and key management. how granular is your RBAC?
[28:10] Ava Chen: RBAC supports role templates (admin, dev, ops, auditor) and custom roles with fine-grained perms across models, routes, and log access. SSO via SAML/OIDC supported, SCIM provisioning available for groups.
[28:34] Priya Kaur: can we get an example policy that denies key management for dev role?
[28:38] Samir Patel: yes, we'll include a sample deny-list policy in the RBAC guide.

[32:00] Liam O'Connor: encryption at rest — are embeddings and KV cache encrypted with same keys as model checkpoints?
[32:08] Ava Chen: embeddings and KV cache are encrypted at rest using the account KMS; model checkpoints in our runtime are handled separately, but we can provide key separation controls for enterprise accounts.

[36:00] Priya Kaur: one more — pen test called out some rate-limiting bypasses on older routes. what's your throttling enforcement?
[36:10] Samir Patel: we've hardened rate-limiting on the control plane and data plane; older routes in the sandbox had laxer defaults. production enforces per-token and per-route quotas with dynamic throttling. we'll push sandbox config changes.

[40:00] Jordan Lee: let's do a short recap of decisions and next steps so it's clear.
[40:10] Priya Kaur: agreed. recap?
[40:12] Jordan Lee: recap: 1) Redwood will patch sandbox client and rotate sample tokens (Samir) 2) Dedicated image patched; we'll notify pinned-image customers and offer assistance to upgrade (Ava) 3) Enable customer-managed KMS for Aurora hosted account (Samir to start) 4) Provide SOC2/ISO docs and SDLC artifacts (Ava) 5) Provide RBAC/SSO config guide and sample deny policies (Samir) 6) Share annotated pen-test spreadsheet with per-finding ETA (Jordan)
[40:50] Priya Kaur: that covers it. we'll send Aurora's internal patch approval matrix to help align timelines.

[42:00] Mark DeVries: two administrative items — can we get a statement on responsibility boundaries for hosted vs dedicated in writing? and can you include patch SLAs in the dedicated contract?
[42:12] Jordan Lee: yes to both — we'll produce a short responsibilities doc and include patch SLA language in the dedicated addendum.

[47:00] Sofia Ramos: compliance question — any issues with exporting logs to EU S3 for retention and e-discovery?
[47:10] Ava Chen: supported; we'll provide the playbook and sample IAM role/policy. data residency is achieved by routing logs to a region-specific export endpoint or using Private control plane.

[49:30] Priya Kaur: ok final question — for reporting to our board, we need a timeline for closing all critical findings. can you produce a consolidated remediation timeline?
[49:40] Jordan Lee: yes, Jordan will consolidate and send a timeline in the spreadsheet — include per-finding ETAs and owners.

[50:00] Jordan Lee: cool, thanks everyone. we'll action the items, share artifacts, and schedule the follow-up in two weeks. appreciate the thoroughness.
[50:12] Priya Kaur: thanks all.
[50:15] Mark DeVries: thanks.
[50:18] Samir Patel: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (kernel vs colonel, KMS spelled out inconsistently). recorded duration 52 minutes.
